A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, Markovian framework, core estimator, and simulation studies despite the changed title. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of a two-state MDP, a hospital queue, and NYC ridesharing, including repeated-trial results and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original simulations and adds empirical variance-estimator validation and negative treatment-perturbation results.

M1.justification: The fixed-k reward-sum estimator is retained and renamed TPG. v2 adds a nonstationary HAC variance estimator and an explicit data-dependent truncation-selection algorithm, substantially extending the procedure to uncertainty estimation and adaptive tuning (Section 6 and Appendix B).

E1.justification: The two-state MDP, hospital queue, and NYC ridesharing domains remain. Appendix G.1 extends synthetic test scenarios to treatment kernels shifting probability in the opposite direction: Figure 7 adds negative perturbations of -0.1 and -0.3, whereas v1 Figure 6 contains only positive perturbations.

E2.justification: The original DM, stationary DQ, OPE, and bias-corrected switchback comparisons are retained; untruncated DQ is renamed PG. The new variance-validation comparison in v2 Figure 3 introduces Monte Carlo variance estimates as a reference for the proposed HAC estimator.

E3.justification: v2 adds a protocol comparing HAC and Monte Carlo asymptotic variance across truncation sizes through k = 20. It also attributes the queueing choice of k = 4 or 5 to Appendix B's selection algorithm. Existing simulation horizons and switchback intervals remain unchanged; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds variance-estimator validation across k in Figure 3 and extends the two-state sensitivity analysis to negative perturbations in Figure 7(i–p). Existing positive-perturbation panels and switchback-interval analyses are retained, while Figure 2's mixing-rate sensitivity curves are revised.

E5.justification: v1 reports simulation standard deviations and boxplots without a practical single-trajectory variance estimator. v2 introduces HAC uncertainty estimation, asymptotic normality, and mean-plus-or-minus-SE reporting in Figure 3. The existing 1,000, 500, and 100 simulation repetition counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 2's MAE curves change under the same described settings: for k = 5 near mixing rate 1, MAE changes from approximately 39% to 34%. Table 1 and the original case-study boxplots remain unchanged. v2 adds HAC-versus-Monte-Carlo findings and eight negative-perturbation result panels, and omits the previously reported LSTD-OPE standard deviation of 0.45.

T1.justification: v2 adds Assumptions 2–3, Theorem 2 on fixed-k asymptotic normality and HAC consistency, and supporting definitions, lemmas, and proofs in Appendices D.2 and F.2–F.4. The original Theorem 1 bounds remain. Section 5 also replaces the explicit truncated-bias decomposition with an untruncated expression that omits the displayed mixing-bias term.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add central claims concerning a CLT, consistent variance estimation from one nonstationary trajectory, statistical inference, and data-driven truncation selection. These substantially extend v1's principal contribution of low-bias, low-variance point estimation.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of mean-stability requirements and cautions that truncation selection must handle a non-monotone bias bound. It removes v1's explicit concluding limitations concerning covariates, doubly robust extensions, and formal comparisons with alternative experimental designs. Existing interpretations of the queueing and ridesharing results largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B documents the selection grid, stability threshold with example 1.96, stopping rule, and DM fallback. Appendix G.1 clarifies the treatment perturbation component by component, and the advertised code pointer changes to TPG-Estimator. Existing hardware and simulator implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Arlotto and Steele (2016) and Hansen (1992) for the CLT/HAC development, removes Chamandy (2016) and Poiani et al. (2023), and reframes stationary DQ within the broader policy-gradient viewpoint. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially compressed and rewritten, the introduction recasts the argument around TPG, Sections 4–5 reorganize the explanation, and the conclusion is rewritten. Appendix proofs are regrouped, including moving the mixing lemma's proof into a separate lemma-proof appendix. This constitutes a broad narrative revision beyond terminology changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds the HAC comparison figure, expands the appendix sensitivity display from eight to sixteen panels, relocates Figure 1 earlier, and changes Figure 2's proportions. Existing case-study plots receive TPG labels, and captions are refined. The overall visual style and table structure remain stable.

improvement.justification: v2 adds potentially valuable inference and tuning procedures with new empirical support. However, Appendix F.4 invokes Delta_T = o(T^(-1/3)), stronger than Assumption 3's stated condition on Delta_T squared. Algorithm 1 stops at the first acceptable k while its explanation claims the largest, and Section 5 loses v1's explicit truncated-bias decomposition. These issues affect the main new benefits and mathematical clarity, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
